title: Standalone workstation hardening: intent-driven, unattended ISO

questions.description: Already decided in grilling: one intent file per machine/person generates both blueprint and kickstart; inventory stays builder-only (gir, tinybot). The intent file holds no plaintext secrets (password is generated per ISO), but it names a person and their machine.
questions.recommendedAnswer: profiles/<name>.yml, gitignored; committed examples in profiles/examples/*.yml. Run: ansible-playbook playbooks/build.yml -e @profiles/<name>.yml

options.label: profiles/<name>.yml (gitignored) + committed profiles/examples/
profiles/<name>.yml, all committed
Outside the repo (e.g. ~/.config/syncopated/profiles/), path passed in

questions.prompt: How is the intent schema defined and enforced?
questions.description: The schema is the durable contract a future CLI/web UI writes against, so it should be machine-readable outside Ansible.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Canonical JSON Schema (schema/intent.schema.json) validated at play start with ansible.utils.validate (jsonschema engine); role keeps meta/argument_specs.yml for its own derived variables.

options.label: JSON Schema file, validated by ansible.utils.validate at play start
Ansible meta/argument_specs.yml only
JSON Schema canonical, argument_specs generated from it

questions.prompt: Which fields belong in intent schema v1?
questions.description: Anything not listed becomes a role-derived value (repos, sources, volume sizes, pre_tasks plumbing, output names).

options.label: distro (e.g. rocky-10.2) + arch
hostname
hardware/stack → components (nvidia, cuda, intel-graphics, audio…)
hardening: none | cis-l2-workstation | pci-dss | hipaa
disk: size_gib, encrypt, tmp mode, optional serial pin
users: name, gecos, groups, optional uid, optional ssh pubkey
locale, keyboard, timezone
remote_logging block (enabled false by default)
extra_packages + package_pins

questions.prompt: How are the user's supplementary groups chosen?
questions.description: An artist workstation needs audio/video/render; containers-virt implies libvirt; wheel gives sudo (root is locked).
questions.recommendedAnswer: Components declare the groups they need (new optional component key user_groups, e.g. containers-virt → libvirt); the role unions them with wheel and any groups listed in intent.

options.label: Derived from components + wheel + intent extras
Only what the intent file lists
Fixed set: wheel, audio, video, render

questions.prompt: Safety before the unattended install wipes the disk?
questions.description: A fully unattended ISO erases the chosen disk (NVMe first, then largest) as soon as it boots. If it's booted on the wrong machine, that data is gone.
questions.recommendedAnswer: 30-second tty countdown naming disk model/size with an abort key (no keypress = proceed), plus an optional disk serial pin in intent that aborts on mismatch.

options.label: %pre countdown naming the disk; any key aborts, timeout proceeds
Optional disk.serial in intent; mismatch aborts
Boot menu default is 'Troubleshoot', install must be picked
No safety: the ISO is personal

questions.prompt: Where does the 'audit volume nearly full' warning appear?
questions.description: Triggered by auditd space_left_action=exec at 25% free. With rotation it is a backstop.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Persistent GNOME critical notification (stays until dismissed, re-shown each login while the condition holds), motd + Cockpit banner, and a journal entry.

options.label: Persistent GNOME critical notification for wheel users
motd / Cockpit banner
Journal entry (priority warning)
Mail to root (postfix is installed by CIS)

questions.prompt: HIPAA keeps the full audit rule set. Same 512 MB rotation cap?
questions.description: Full rules on a desktop ran ~280 MB/h; 512 MB is ~2 h of history. For the assessment lab, more history helps correlate violations with agent runs.
questions.recommendedAnswer: HIPAA: 64 MB × 32 = 2 GiB cap on a 10 GiB audit LV; CIS/PCI: 32 MB × 16 = 512 MB cap on 4 GiB.

options.label: HIPAA 2 GiB cap / 10 GiB LV; CIS+PCI 512 MB / 4 GiB
Same 512 MB / 4 GiB for all

questions.prompt: What happens to today's per-variant playbooks?
questions.description: playbooks/osbuild-rocky-iso-*.yml, osbuild-almalinux-iso*.yml, osbuild-rocky-cuda-container.yml, osbuild.yml. bootc/container paths are out of scope.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Convert each ISO playbook into profiles/examples/<variant>.yml, assert the generated blueprint matches today's output (except the intended audit/disk/user changes), then delete the ISO playbooks. Leave container/bootc playbooks untouched.

options.label: Convert ISO playbooks to example intents, regression-check, delete them
Keep them as thin wrappers that load an example intent
Leave them; new path lives alongside

questions.description: No log server and no spare hardware assumed.
questions.recommendedAnswer: All automated items, plus one manual install on the test laptop.

options.label: Generation tests: schema validation, disk-size math, rendered kickstart/tailoring (pytest/bats), ksvalidator
image-builder manifest depsolve for every example intent
Throwaway systemd-journal-remote container receives uploads (e2e for the toggle)
Unattended QEMU/libvirt install of the CIS ISO: no prompts, layout + auditd.conf + oscap scan checked
Manual install on the test laptop, 48 h uptime, /var/log/audit stays under cap
